english: The range of $f$ is $(-\infty,\alpha]\cup[\beta,\infty)$, where $\alpha<\beta$. Then the value of $\alpha+\beta$ is ______.
hindi: द्वारा परिभाषित है। $f$ का परिसर $(-\infty,\alpha]\cup[\beta,\infty)$ है, जहाँ $\alpha<\beta$ है। तब $\alpha+\beta$ का मान ______ है।
solution: $y=0$ is taken at $t=-2$. For $y\neq0$, real $t$ needs $(2y+2)^{2}+4y(3y+4)\ge0\Rightarrow4y^{2}+6y+1\ge0$

$t=-1$ or $3$ never satisfies the quadratic (the left side equals $-10$ and $-2$ there), so no value is lost: range $=\left(-\infty,\dfrac{-3-\sqrt5}{4}\right]\cup\left[\dfrac{-3+\sqrt5}{4},\infty\right)$
solution_full: The bases $\dfrac x8$ and $2x$ are positive and differ from $1$ exactly when $x>0,\ x\neq8,\ x\neq\dfrac12$, which is the given domain.
Let $t=\log_2x$; as $x$ runs over the domain, $t$ runs over $\mathbb{R}\setminus\{3,-1\}$.
By the product, quotient and power rules and the change of base: $\log_{x/8}(4x)=\dfrac{\log_2 4+\log_2x}{\log_2x-\log_2 8}=\dfrac{t+2}{t-3}$ and $\log_{2x}4=\dfrac{2}{1+t}$.
So $f=\dfrac{2(t+2)}{(t-3)(t+1)}$. A value $y$ is in the range iff $2(t+2)=y(t^{2}-2t-3)$ has a root $t\neq3,-1$, i.e. iff $yt^{2}-(2y+2)t-(3y+4)=0$ has such a root.
At $t=3$ the left side is $9y-6y-6-3y-4=-10\neq0$; at $t=-1$ it is $y+2y+2-3y-4=-2\neq0$. So the excluded values of $t$ are never roots and remove nothing.
$y=0$: the equation is $-2t-4=0$, $t=-2$, allowed; so $0$ is in the range.
$y\neq0$: a real root exists iff the discriminant $(2y+2)^{2}+4y(3y+4)=16y^{2}+24y+4\ge0$, i.e. $4y^{2}+6y+1\ge0$.
The roots of $4y^{2}+6y+1=0$ are $\dfrac{-3\pm\sqrt5}{4}$, so the range is $\left(-\infty,\dfrac{-3-\sqrt5}{4}\right]\cup\left[\dfrac{-3+\sqrt5}{4},\infty\right)$ (it contains $0$, as it must).
originality_note: New: a product of two variable-base logarithms reduces, with t = log_2 x, to a quadratic-over-quadratic rational function whose range has a gap with irrational ends; the sum of the ends is read off by Vieta from the discriminant inequality (way 5). Closest known: range of log_2 x + log_x 2 by AM-GM, and range of rational functions by the discriminant method. Different because: the gap ends are irrational, the excluded t-values must be checked against the quadratic, and the asked quantity comes from Vieta on the discriminant.

concept_use.Logarithmic identities: product, quotien: Product, quotient, power and change-of-base rules turn both factors into rational functions of t = log_2 x.
concept_use.Range by inverse method, boundedness, AM: The range is found by the inverse/discriminant method: y is attained iff 4y^2 + 6y + 1 >= 0, after checking the excluded t-values.
